headline: I was curious how X is fighting AI slop, so I looked at its open-source algorithm. It has a behavioral model called TweetSpamBot that analyzes up to 512 recent account actions, looking at signals like posting bursts, quote-post behavior, timing, and normal browsing or dwell between actions. The model is trained to recognize patterns such as: → TWEET_CREATE_BURST → QUOTE_TWEET_SPAMMER → CONTENT_AMPLIFIER A high score on the above can feed into an account challenge but doesn't seem to downrank the slop posts themselves. I think the gap here is that the model doesn’t read the actual post content. So a sophisticated AI content mill can still post slop all day long: 1. Find viral posts 2. Quote tweet with the same template each time: hook → numbers → backstory → takeaway 3. Repeat 10+ times a day across unrelated topics If @X doesn't want to become like LinkedIn, I think it should consider looking at accounts that repeatedly turn unrelated viral posts into the same templated quote tweet slop at high volume. Right now the guardrails above are too easy to bypass.
